discoveries.hypothesis: When I give a clue to another player, the recipient must immediately play one card (the turn is consumed by giving the clue and the recipient's play follows as part of that resolution).
discoveries.test: Give a legal clue to a player and observe whether that player is required to play immediately and which slots they choose.
discoveries.prediction: The referee will forward the clue and then the indicated player will play a single card as part of the same exchange; their chosen slot will be executed immediately.
evidence: After I sent [clue: player 1, B] the log says 'Forwarded to player 1: player 1, colour B. They played slot 2: ['B', 1]; built.'
Subsequent clues were similarly forwarded and immediately followed by the recipient playing a slot.
instructions: When I want a specific player to act, give a single precise clue that singles out the intended playable slot so their immediate forced play advances the stacks.
Avoid giving ambiguous clues if I need a different player action later because they will be forced to play immediately.

discoveries.hypothesis: A clue must be a single colour or a single rank that actually appears in the recipient's hand; the system enforces this.
discoveries.test: Attempt to give a clue with a colour or rank not present in the recipient's current hand and observe rejection.
discoveries.prediction: The referee will not accept a clue that does not match any card in the recipient's hand.
evidence: Instructions in the log state 'A clue must contain only a recipient and one colour or rank actually in that hand.' and all clues given in play targeted attributes present in that hand.
instructions: Only attempt clues that match at least one visible card in the recipient's hand; if I try otherwise the action should be invalid.

discoveries.hypothesis: When a clue is given, the recipient receives marks on every slot that matches the clued colour or rank (not just one).
discoveries.test: Give a colour or rank clue where the recipient has multiple cards matching that attribute and observe whether all matching slots are marked.
discoveries.prediction: The referee will mark every matching slot and the recipient will play with full knowledge of all marked slots.
evidence: Instructions assert 'The recipient receives all matching slot marks.' and a given clue to player 1 for colour B marked the single matching B1; behavior supports multi-mark rule as a general mechanism.
instructions: Use clues that mark all matching slots when I intend the recipient to disambiguate among multiple possibilities; plan around the fact that all matches will be revealed to them simultaneously.

discoveries.hypothesis: Clue tokens decrement when I give a clue; they are a limited resource (four initial) and the system enforces the count.
discoveries.test: Give clues repeatedly and watch the token count decrease; attempt to give a clue when tokens are zero and observe rejection.
discoveries.prediction: The token count shown in game state will drop by one per clue; when tokens are zero the referee will disallow clues.
evidence: Tokens started at 4 and dropped to 3, then 2, then 1 following the clues I gave.
The log displays 'Tokens 4' then later 'Tokens 3' etc.
instructions: When I consider giving a clue, first check token count; conserve tokens for safe forced plays if possible.
If tokens are low, prefer clues that are guaranteed-to-play rather than ambiguous hints.

discoveries.hypothesis: Playing a card that is not the next rank for its colour will be treated as a discard (no build) and penalize the team by not increasing score.
discoveries.test: Play a slot known not to match the required next rank on its colour stack and observe whether it is discarded and whether score changes.
discoveries.prediction: The card will be discarded and score will not increase; the card will be removed from the player's hand.
evidence: My final action [play: 1] executed on my own turn resulted in the slot's card being discarded and no increase in stacks; final referee resolution: 'You played slot 1: ['R', 2]; discarded.'
instructions: Do not play from my hand unless I have information that the slot is playable; if forced to act without safe clues, prefer to give a clue to someone else if tokens allow.
If I must play with no safe information, accept the risk that it could be a discard and avoid wasting tokens trying to confirm unknowns.

discoveries.hypothesis: A review request consumes a round, uses a clue-like action, does not reveal unmarked cards, and only reports the clue marks on my hand.
discoveries.test: Call the review action [review: 0] during a turn and observe what is revealed and whether it consumes a turn.
discoveries.prediction: The referee will show the current marks on my hand without revealing unmarked cards and will consume the player's action for that round.
evidence: The rules state '[review: 0] requests a review of your clue marks; reviews must not reveal unmarked cards and use a round.' (this text was present in the game prompts).
instructions: Use review if I need to confirm what marks I already have when the board state is unclear, but expect it to consume my turn and not expose unknown cards.

playbook.strategy:
When I have a safe immediate build visible in another player's hand, give a single precise clue (colour or rank) that uniquely identifies that playable slot so they are forced to play it and score a point.
When giving a clue, always ensure it matches at least one card in the recipient's hand; do not attempt illegal clues.
When tokens are low, prioritize clues that guarantee productive immediate plays rather than ambiguous information.
When I can mark multiple identical attributes in a hand, use that to communicate which among several cards are candidates; remember every match will be marked.
Never play from my own hand unless I have information that the slot is playable; if no safe clues exist and tokens allow, prefer to give a clue to someone else rather than risk a discard.
If forced to act with no safe information and tokens are unavailable, accept that a play may be discarded and avoid spending tokens to 'double-check' unknowns.
Use a review only when I need to confirm which marks I already have and I'm willing to spend my action for the round; do not expect it to reveal unmarked cards.
Conserve clue tokens early to enable forced safe builds later; track tokens carefully before deciding to clue.
If a decision requires revealing a particular card in another hand to chain future plays, give the clue that marks all matches so teammates can deduce context from which slots are marked.
When a clue will force a player to play, plan the board state after that play (stacks and remaining hands) because the forced play is immediate and may change available safe plays.
